chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

Concerning a slave who entered into a contract of manumission over himself and his wealth, and he had a female slave, and it had been stipulated upon him that he should not marry, then he freed the female slave and married her, he said: “It is not proper for him to make any disposition in his wealth except a meal of food, and his marriage is invalid and rejected.”
It was said: “If his master came to know of his marriage and did not say anything?” He said: “If he remains silent when he knows that, then he has approved it.”
It was said: “If the mukātab is emancipated, do you see that he should renew his marriage contract, or proceed upon the first marriage?” He said: “He proceeds upon his marriage.”

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: a slave under a manumission contract
key_terms.كَاتَبَ: entered into a contract of manumission
key_terms.مَالِهِ: his property or wealth subject to legal restriction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mukātab who frees and marries his slave woman without explicit permission from his master?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a mukātab whose financial and marital actions were restricted by the terms of his contract. It states that his marriage is initially invalid without the master's approval, but the master's informed silence counts as approval, and after emancipation the marriage continues without needing renewal.
